conflicts.fact: Chemical identity/classification of CAN fertiliser (and whether it is a normal salt made by neutralisation)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 calls CAN NH₄NO₃, a normal salt, and also a 'Ca(NO₃)₂ / NH₄NO₃ mixture'. Lesson 2 uses NH₄NO₃ to represent CAN. Lesson 5 says CAN is 'ammonium nitrate — soluble, made by neutralisation'. Lessons 6 and 8 treat CAN as deliquescent. The sequence is inconsistent about whether CAN is a single compound or a mixture, and about its composition.

conflicts.fact: Which salt explains the CAN clumping / classification of CaCl₂ behaviour
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says CaCl₂ (not CAN) is hygroscopic and 'may explain the clumping behaviour observed in CAN fertiliser'. Lesson 6 uses CaCl₂ as a stand-in and lists CAN as deliquescent in its own right. Lesson 4 also links the washing soda efflorescence to CO₂ production, but washing soda loses water of crystallisation rather than reacting with acid.

conflicts.fact: Product of efflorescence of washing soda
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 gives Na₂CO₃·10H₂O → Na₂CO₃ + 10H₂O (anhydrous). Lesson 8 gives Na₂CO₃·10H₂O → Na₂CO₃·H₂O + 9H₂O (monohydrate), losing nine of ten waters, while also saying 'anhydrous or monohydrate'.

conflicts.fact: Definition of deliquescent vs hygroscopic and classification of CAN
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 groups 'deliquescent/hygroscopic' together and says CaCl₂ is 'deliquescent/hygroscopic'. Lesson 8 defines hygroscopic as absorbing moisture without dissolving and deliquescent as dissolving, while describing CAN as 'deliquescent (or strongly hygroscopic)', which is inconsistent with that distinction. Lesson 6 says NaCl is 'neither hygroscopic nor efflorescent'.

conflicts.fact: Anchor phenomenon: washing soda location and time
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: washing soda on lab bench; Lesson 8 consistent. But Lesson 6 says washing soda lost water to 'dry air' while the storeroom is described as 'humid'; Lesson 8 says laboratory air is 'drier' while using 'humid storeroom'. Mostly consistent, minor.

Lesson 2: insoluble except sodium, potassium and ammonium. Lesson 8: insoluble except ammonium carbonate and Group 1 carbonates (broader than Na/K). Also Lesson 2 says lead sulphate and barium sulphate are the exceptions for sulphates, while Lessons 3 and 8 add slightly soluble CaSO₄.

conflicts.fact: Number of preparation methods and the lesson in which the flow chart began
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 overview calls a 'four-method summary flow chart' but lists five routes (direct synthesis, acid + metal, acid + metal oxide, acid + base, acid + carbonate); Lesson 4 model says the chart was begun in Lesson 3 but teacher says 'since Lesson 2'. Lesson 5 says 'all four preparation methods studied so far'.

conflicts.fact: DQB duration and final lesson number
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the DQB stays for all 8 lessons and 'By Lesson 30 it should be nearly full of answers'; the unit has 8 lessons.
